titleStmt.title: Surface Code Threshold Estimates for Near-Term Devices

analytic.title: Surface Code Threshold Estimates for Near-Term Devices

abstract.p: We estimate surface-code thresholds under realistic noise.

div.head: Introduction
div.p: Fault-tolerant quantum computing relies on error-correcting codes.
The surface code remains a leading candidate for near-term devices.

div.head: Methods
div.p: We simulate a distance-d surface code under depolarizing noise.

div.head: Noise model
div.p: Independent X and Z errors are applied after each gate.

div.head: Decoder
div.p: Minimum-weight perfect matching decodes the syndrome.

div.head: Results
div.p: Threshold behaviour appears near one percent physical error rate.

div.head: Threshold estimates
div.p: The extrapolated threshold is 1.1 percent under our noise model.
Supplemental curves for distance five through eleven are included.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: Near-term devices can approach the surface-code threshold.
